sections.content:
32,115 people

were counted on the census as "clergy" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Members of the clergy provide spiritual motivation and guidance, conduct worship according to the form of service of a particular faith or denomination, and perform related functions associated with religious beliefs and practices.

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "clergy" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "clergy", 16.5% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "clergy" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.title: The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years
sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "clergy" included:

  • psychotherapists and cognitive behaviour therapists
  • company secretaries and administrators
  • bus and coach drivers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "clergy" there were more men than women (71.2% compared with 28.8%).

This means "clergy" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "business, media and public service professionals".

Men made up 71.2% and women made up 28.8% of "clergy"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "clergy" included:

  • photographers, audio-visual and broadcasting equipment operators
  • estimators, valuers and assessors
  • upholsterers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "clergy" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "clergy" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "clergy", 11.4% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (74.8% compared with 25.2%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (83.1%) than self-employed (16.9%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
